analysis_refs.heading: 2. Scope
analysis_refs.text:
- Free to read: Project Gutenberg (local metadata import), Open Textbook
  Library and the bounded Book Dash catalog (owner-approved source expansion). Other free versions (LibriVox, Wikisource) appear only on detail
  pages as separate items, when a source links them.
- Papers: OpenAlex (when its key and budget are verified), Europe PMC, DOAJ,
  arXiv.
- Children's stories: the reviewed pilot set only, labelled as such.
- The library book page gains an "Also free to read" section.
- Desktop and mobile layouts, all three reading lights.

analysis_refs.heading: FCD01: contract decisions
analysis_refs.text:
- Content keys use `fcd:v1:<source>:<record>`; Gutenberg records are positive
  integer IDs; Europe PMC records include their source (`MED`, `PMC`, `PPR`).
  A DOI is an identifier, never an app key. Versions, translations, chapters and
  recordings retain distinct source-native keys. No fuzzy-title merge.
- Reviewed StoryWeaver translations use distinct native story IDs. The pilot
  requires English/Hindi/Tamil records with original credits, publisher levels
  and per-record review evidence before enablement.
- An omitted `kinds` searches books/learning resources. Paper searches supply
  paper kinds explicitly. Mixed book/paper requests are reported unsupported;
  the API never silently omits one requested scope.
- Search and resolve both accept `country` (ISO alpha-2 or absent/unknown) and
  language context. An observation for one explicit country does not establish
  availability in another. Gutenberg's US rights statement is retained with a
  generic country-rules prompt, not turned into a global legal claim.
- A reading action requires an explicit per-location `free_full_text` claim,
  positive evidence field/source/time, a safe supplied HTTP(S) URL, and an
  observation no older than 24 hours. Stale, missing, contradictory or
  country-mismatched observations become unknown; fetch failure is not absence.
  Reuse licence and free reading remain distinct. Missing licence never becomes
  an invented Creative Commons licence.
- `not_selected` means the planner did not query this source; `disabled` means
  it is not connected. `ok` with zero results is distinct from timeout,
  unavailable, throttled and quota-exhausted. Counts describe loaded items,
  never a federated global total.
- Default results contain anonymous free full text and a separately labelled verified free-account group (owner clarification 2026-11-01). An explicit unclear group may
  contain unknown/metadata-only items with labelled source links; previews,
  borrowing, unknown-price registration and restricted access stay excluded in v1.
- Source cursors remain server-owned. Browser tokens bind query, context,
  policy/index revisions and expiry. Shared live quota reservation and page
  advancement must pass a two-instance test before a live source is enabled.
  A memory implementation is a development/test adapter only; store failure
  disables uncapped live dispatch while keeping local metadata searchable.

analysis_refs.heading: Actual sources and browser
analysis_refs.text:
[Direct source probes](evidence/2026-11-03/direct-live-probes.json) use official
APIs and the existing OpenAlex key, without store bindings. Mathematics selects
OpenAlex; malaria selects Europe PMC. Both return current readable metadata,
resolve exact native records live and continue to another page. A Europe PMC
continuation overlapped one record, confirming why live paging is not a frozen,
globally duplicate-free snapshot. The browser removes repeated source keys.

analysis_refs.heading: Historical shared-store profile (superseded)
analysis_refs.text:
The planner selects at most three live providers. Biomedical terms prefer
Europe PMC; general queries prefer the broad source and arXiv; DOAJ supplies
OA journal coverage. Recognized arXiv identifiers select arXiv. Sources not
chosen are explicit and can be searched independently from the source sheet.
DOIs select DOI-capable indexes; PMCIDs select Europe PMC using its PMCID field,
preserving the article's native MED identity. Bare versioned legacy arXiv IDs
also route directly to arXiv.
Language context is only supported by the broad adapter today; other paper
sources report unsupported rather than silently ignoring it.

analysis_refs.heading: Free-content production release
analysis_refs.text:
**Current revision (2026-11-03):** the owner authorized the
[simple free live plan](SIMPLE_LIVE_PLAN.md), #156. Release/hosted verification is
tracked in #159. Europe PMC/OpenAlex can run directly with no data store; the
blanket Redis gate is superseded. This release must retain verified free-budget
guards and existing account settings. The November 1 evidence below records the
initial book release, rather than the current paper prerequisites.

analysis_refs.heading: Product requirements
analysis_refs.text:
- Search one selected paper source live. General searches use OpenAlex;
  biomedical searches and PMCIDs use Europe PMC. The Sources sheet switches
  sources. Explicit selection never silently searches a different source.
- Show more carries the provider's paging token in a signed browser token.
  Opening a result resolves its native record directly at that provider.
- No new database, Redis account, paid integration, shared cache or stored search
  session. Existing account features/resources are outside this change.
- Direct arXiv/DOAJ automation stays off because its aggregate pacing rules need
  coordination across deployments. Offer searches on their source websites;
  these connectors do not block other paper sources.
- Keep current source identities, verified free-reading rules, credits, versions,
  separate translations, source errors and browser shelf behavior.

analysis_refs.heading: Cost and limits
analysis_refs.text:
Europe PMC uses its public API. OpenAlex uses the existing server-only key;
verify its free allowance, accepted endpoint pricing and zero prepaid balance
before dispatch. Exhaustion, paid balances or unknown policy stop the request.
No paid fallback or paid infrastructure is introduced. Normal hosting usage
continues under the existing Vercel plan; future hosting costs are not guaranteed
to be zero.

analysis_refs.heading: Configuration and delivery
analysis_refs.text:
Keep the existing discovery flag and strong cursor signer. Enable Europe PMC
and optionally OpenAlex with its key. Remove Redis and per-source application
daily/minute budget variables from active setup. No client-exposed credentials
or database migration.

analysis_refs.heading: Evidence and limits
analysis_refs.text:
- The comparison fixtures are explicitly synthetic for papers/stories; they do
  not establish source access or represent the actual reviewed children's set.
  Their metadata is isolated in `client/e2e/free-content-ui-fixture.js`.
- The [actual-source app flows](evidence/2026-11-01/ui-review/actual-source-flow/expanded-sources-app-flow.json)
  separately exercise the real Tamil StoryWeaver record and Book Dash edition:
  search → detail → supplied source URL → save → reload → reopen, on desktop and
  phone, including 320px/200% text. Their credits and free-account condition are
  preserved. No source account was created and post-login reading is untested.
- Sources, counts, levels and available relations differ from the board samples.
  Only source-supplied versions/downloads/relations render; no v1/v2 list, recording,
  translation, cover art or licence is inferred to imitate sample data.
- The shared four-tab shell, desktop navigation rail and browser safe-area
  handling remain the existing app. The source sheet keeps its shared Close
  control. Catalog-subset disclosure and the owner-approved free-account group
  add necessary content beyond the original sample boards.
- Recent query history is bounded and lost on reload. It is not written to
  local storage, an account, analytics or a server history store.
- A fresh Europe PMC request on the current local API exceeded the five-second
  source deadline. The actual UI rendered an unavailable alert and no empty-copy
  claim. Earlier successful live-paper flows remain dated evidence, not a claim
  that the external service answered this later probe.
- The streamed-loading fixture uses the same local origin and `nosniff`/no-store
  headers as the app API. This avoids engine-dependent buffering/routing in the
  temporary review endpoint; it keeps the real progress assertions.
- Automated contrast/layout checks do not replace a screen-reader usability
  session. Firefox was not run locally. Remote CI covers WebKit as well.
- Hosted feature enablement, Redis-backed hosted paper journeys and the first
  scheduled refresh remain the previously recorded release gates. No flags,
  hosted credentials, storage or production deployment settings were changed.

analysis_refs.heading: Final source and refresh checks
analysis_refs.text:
[HEAD/header-only sampling](evidence/2026-11-01/host-head-checks.json) returned
200 from the textbook, DOAJ publisher, arXiv and Europe PMC hosts. It found a
Gutenberg legacy HTML 404; GET response headers confirmed it. The supplied direct
HTML and EPUB routes returned 200. Importer v2 removes virtual HTML links and
uses supplied direct HTML/landing URLs; a fresh 1,000-record import and runtime
audit passed. The primary location's licence and downloads now stay together;
other hosts/versions retain their own licence, and retraction flags appear on
direct detail visits. No full-text content was stored.

analysis_refs.heading: 5. Search and item resolution
analysis_refs.text:
1. Validate query length, filters, page size (initial max 40), country and cursor binding. Detect ISBN/DOI/arXiv/PMCID before broad search. Country is access context, not legal assurance.
2. Choose providers by user scope/capabilities. Books start from local catalogs; papers use OpenAlex when configured plus at most two relevant specialists. Without the broad index, disclose narrower DOAJ/Europe PMC/arXiv coverage.
3. Use shared cached results. Acquire global quota tokens for uncached requests; arXiv pacing includes all replicas/jobs. Skip with explicit status if the queue cannot run before the deadline.
4. Bound fan-out: proposed 5-second total search deadline, shorter per-provider limits where feasible, at most 3 live providers and one source page each. These are design targets, not measured guarantees. Busy arXiv queues cannot delay every result indefinitely.
5. Map, filter, reconcile and rank. Avoid detail requests for every hit; resolve uncertain access for bounded visible candidates or on item open. Unknown candidates cannot be advertised as free.
6. Return items, source statuses and freshness. Empty, timeout, throttled, quota-exhausted, unsupported and disabled differ. If all sources fail with no local/cached result, return retriable unavailable, not zero matches.
7. On item open, enrich locations as needed; surface editions/versions and host actions. Cache bibliography separately from access observations.

analysis_refs.heading: Phase A — contract and two vertical slices
analysis_refs.text: Define manifests/model/access eligibility/shared budgeting/routes. Implement Gutenberg import/local search and Europe PMC live search to prove both paths. Add cards/details/host actions behind a flag and sanitized fixtures under source terms.

analysis_refs.heading: What the original checks established
analysis_refs.text: Structured responses were obtained from Google Books (using the configured key), Open Library, Internet Archive, DOAJ, OpenAlex, Crossref, arXiv, Europe PMC, CORE, Zenodo, HAL, Wikisource, Library of Congress, and LibriVox. Gutenberg RDF and DOAB record/harvesting responses also worked. OAPEN's OAI service identification worked; a record import was not exercised.
